pitch_detail.notes: From a horn near the summit, rappel straight down the northeast side of the summit block. These are the first three of about five single-rope rappels (roughly 400 ft in all) that lead onto the ledge system. Inspect every anchor: the stations are slung tat on rock, not bolts.

A short, grassy traverse east across exposed ground brings you to the next rock rib and the station for the remaining rappels. Unroped slips here are the danger; keep the party close and move one at a time where it steepens.
Two more rappels put you onto the East Ledges proper. Some parties make a sixth rappel in place of a little downclimbing; either works on a single rope.

Traverse east along sandy, grassy and loose ledges well below the ridge crest, crossing about five rock ribs with short 4th-class moves at each. After the first two ribs there are usually a higher and a lower set of cairns marking the easiest crossing. Stay near one level: too low runs into cliffs above the Boston Glacier, too high into steeper, more corrugated ribs and gullies. The ground is largely unprotectable.

At the end of the ledges a short gully climbs back up to the East Ridge crest at the saddle beside the solitary gendarme. Following the higher line of cairns lets a party skip the 4th-class red gully at the end and scramble up blocks to the crest instead.
pitch_detail.pitch: Gully to the East Ridge crest

pitch_detail.notes: From the crest, descend the East Ridge's standard approach line into Boston Basin: high-friction granite slabs strewn with loose grit and pebbles, then a loose gully. Move from one sheltered spot to the next so no one is below a partner when rocks are knocked down.

wa_forbidden_peak_east_ledges.overview: The East Ledges (also called the 'NE Ledge' in older and casual usage - a naming overlap that has caused confusion with the distinct, genuinely technical Northeast Face ice route on the same aspect) is Forbidden Peak's most commonly used descent off the summit. It is not a recommended ascent line: nearly all documentation describes downclimbing or rappelling it, not climbing up it. The terrain is loose, mostly unprotectable 3rd-to-4th-class ledges and ribs, used almost exclusively by parties who summited via the West Ridge, East Ridge (Direct), North Ridge, or the Northeast Face and are looking for a descent that avoids reversing their up-route.
wa_forbidden_peak_east_ledges.approach: Reached only from the summit of Forbidden Peak after climbing another route (West Ridge, East Ridge Direct, North Ridge, or the Northeast Face ice route) - there is no independent trailhead approach to the East Ledges as an ascent line, since it is used almost exclusively as a descent.
wa_forbidden_peak_east_ledges.beta: From a horn near the summit, make the first of five single-rope rappels (roughly 400 ft total) down the northeast side to a series of ledges. Follow the ledges east - mostly 3rd class with short 4th-class moves at rib crossings - across roughly five rock ribs, staying well below the ridge crest, then a short gully leads back up to the ridge crest near the solitary gendarme on the East Ridge. Cairns mark the easiest line across most rib crossings (a higher and lower cairn at each rib), and parties consistently report finding them.
wa_forbidden_peak_east_ledges.descent_text: From a horn near the summit, make the first of five single-rope rappels (roughly 400 ft total) down the northeast side to a series of ledges, then follow the ledges east - mostly 3rd class with short 4th-class moves at rib crossings - across roughly five rock ribs before a short gully leads back up to the East Ridge crest near the solitary gendarme. There is no easy way off Forbidden Peak - this line is unprotectable in places and has had a fatality (1975) on the ledge traverse. Cairns (a higher and lower option at most rib crossings) mark the easiest line; recent parties describe the terrain as more straightforward than its reputation suggests when the cairned line is followed carefully, but conditions and route-finding difficulty vary by party experience and weather. From the gendarme, continue down the East Ridge's standard gully system to Boston Basin.
